# Answering question about Data Types
```{r Answer to #1}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
 
jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, location_state, remote, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::filter(remote == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    posted_at = as.Date(posted_at),
    last_seen_at = as.Date(last_seen_at),
    days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at)
  )
```
# Demo
```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
 
jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, 
last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_at"), as.Date),
                days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at))

jobs
# Q1 -- which cat is remote friendly
# To answer that, the logic would be as follows:
# - Find number of jobs per category
# - Normalize the number of remote jobs by dividing by the total jobs

jobs |>
  # I want to move from unit of analysis being a job posting to a category
  dplyr::group_by(category)|>
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote)
  )

# Among full-time postings, which states have the highest remote share?
# Based on the vote in class, I  will deviate from the answer on the slides

jobs |>
  dplyr::group_by(category, location_state) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote) |> round(digits =2)
  )|>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(remote_share)) |>
  na.omit() # to drop the location_state == NA

```


# Airbnb
```{r Airbnb Data}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb.db")
listings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |>
  tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
dplyr::glimpse(listings)

# 1. How many listings per city
# If the answer is purely based on last class, I can group by City and Count the number of listings in each city 

# This: 
listings |> dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())
# Or this:
listings |> dplyr::count(city)
# Or this: 
table(listings$city)

# 2. What is the median price in each city?

listings |> dplyr::filter(
  room_type == "Entire home/apt" & accommodates >= 4
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price = median(price)
  )

# 3. Add price_per_person = price / accommodates. Which three listings are cheapest per person? Believe them?
  
listings |>
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates) |>
  dplyr::select(city, host_name, name, price, accommodates, price_per_person) |>
  dplyr::arrange(price_per_person)

# 4. Which five host_names have the most listings?
listings |> dplyr::count(host_name, sort = T)
listings |> dplyr::count(host_name, host_id, sort = T)

```
